# StatusPill

Figma: [04e. StatusPill](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-915) · Family: 04 Data Display · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-02

A semantic-tone pill for labeling object attributes - verified, premium, approved, expired - independent of any specific lifecycle. 6 tones (neutral, info, success, warning, error, brand), 2 visual variants (subtle for inline labels, solid for high-emphasis), 2 sizes (sm/md), optional leading icon, bilingual (LTR + RTL). Distinct from IssuanceStatusBadge (lifecycle-specific) - StatusPill is for attributes, states, and categorical labels that live OUTSIDE the issuance lifecycle.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/status-pill/reference.png`

### StatusPill

Read-only pill that labels an attribute or state outside the deal lifecycle (Verified, KYC complete, Pending review, Sharia-certified, Featured) with a semantic tone and optional leading icon. It also serves as the delta chip inside Stat.

Level: atom · Part of: Stat, CardDeal

Use when:
- Investor profile attributes: KYC complete, Qualified investor, Verified
- Document or request states: Draft, Pending, Approved, Rejected, Expired
- Compliance markers on a deal: Sharia-certified, CMA-regulated
- KPI delta inside Stat (↑ 12% success, ↓ 3% error)

Don't use when:
- Deal or issuance lifecycle statuses (Raising, Funded, Late, Defaulted): use IssuanceStatusBadge (Investor)
- Plain categories like sector or document type: use Tag
- Anything removable or toggleable: use Tag Removable
- Deal tier ribbons (Premium, Basic): use dealTags
- A field validation message: use Form Field Helper

Accessibility: Keep 1 to 3 words of text; the icon is decorative and the text conveys meaning; no hover or focus states.

| Size | `size` | variant | sm, md | sm |

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

StatusPill is the semantic-tone label for attributes that aren't part of a defined lifecycle. Where IssuanceStatusBadge maps to 25 specific phases of the Sukuk issuance flow with locked copy and palette, StatusPill is the general-purpose category label - "Verified", "Premium", "Approved", "Expired", "VIP", "Featured". Use it when you need a colored label that says "this thing has this attribute" and the attribute is bounded by a semantic intent (info / success / warning / error) rather than a position in a specific flow.

Two variants for two emphasis levels. Subtle (tinted bg + colored text + soft border) sits comfortably inline within table cells, form labels, and dense layouts without dominating. Solid (saturated bg + white text + no border) makes the pill the focal element - use for callouts, hero KPIs, and surfaces where the status needs to grab attention.

> **Tip:** When to reach for StatusPill vs IssuanceStatusBadge: if the label is one of the 25 specific issuance lifecycle states ("Raising", "Funded", "Defaulted", etc), use IssuanceStatusBadge - its copy and palette are locked to the markdown spec. If the label is a general attribute or state ("Verified", "Featured", "Approved", "Expired"), use StatusPill.

### Tone - semantic intent

Six tones, each anchored to semantic tokens that already exist in Syntropy. Picking a tone is a decision about WHAT THE PILL MEANS - neutral for inert categorization, info for procedural state, success for positive outcomes, warning for things needing attention, error for things gone wrong, brand for editorial promotion.

neutral · default / inert categorization

Use for labels that are categorical but not evaluative - "Draft", "Internal", "Archived", "Unassigned". Subtle uses bg/base + text/muted + border/default; solid uses bg/inverse + text/inverse (dark grey, almost black). Defaults to Icon/info but you'll usually swap to something category-specific or skip the icon entirely.

info · procedural / informational state

Use for in-progress states that aren't positive or negative - "Reviewing", "Processing", "Synced", "Pending". Blue palette signals "this is happening, no action needed yet". Anchored to bg/info-subtle + text/info + border/info (subtle) or bg/info + text/inverse (solid).

success · positive outcome / verified state

Use for completed positive states - "Approved", "Verified", "Active", "Connected", "Paid". Green palette is the most loaded - only reach for it when the state is genuinely positive. Defaults to Icon/check-circle.

warning · needs attention but not broken

Use for states requiring user attention without being errors - "Pending", "Expiring soon", "Action required", "Low balance". Amber palette differentiates from error red - orange-tinted, not red. Defaults to Icon/alert-triangle.

error · something is wrong

Use for failed, rejected, or broken states - "Rejected", "Failed", "Expired", "Blocked", "Disconnected". Red palette is the highest-emphasis tone - use sparingly so it retains weight when it matters. Defaults to Icon/x.

brand · editorial / promotional

Use for labels promoted by Safqah editorial decisions - "Featured", "Premium", "Top performer", "Recommended", "Sharia-certified ★". Safqah green; do NOT use for arbitrary success states (that's `success`). Brand is reserved for surfaces where Safqah itself is endorsing or distinguishing. Defaults to Icon/star.

### Variant - subtle vs solid

Variant is the emphasis decision. Use subtle for inline labels in tables, list rows, form fields, and any layout where the pill is one of many information chunks. Use solid for hero-level callouts, dashboard KPIs, badges that must be the first thing the user sees.

Variant = subtle

Tinted background + colored text + 1px matching border. Lower visual weight. Use inline within tables, list rows, form labels, list of attributes. Reads as informational without dominating.

Variant = solid

Saturated tone background + white text + no border. Higher visual weight. Use for callouts, dashboard hero KPIs, surfaces where the status IS the message.

### Size - sm vs md

Two sizes. The decision is about VISUAL DENSITY in the surrounding layout, not about emphasis (that's what Variant is for).

Size = sm

· Padding 8 / 2 · 12/16 text · 12px icon

· Use in table cells, list row metadata, dense KPI strips

· Reads cleanly at 20px row height

Size = md

· Padding 10 / 4 · 13/16 text · 14px icon

· Default. Use in cards, page headers, deal/issuance details, status sections

· Reads cleanly at 24px row height

### Icon - semantic reinforcement

When HasIcon=true, a leading icon reinforces the tone. Defaults differ per tone - check-circle for success, alert-triangle for warning, x for error, star for brand, info-circle for neutral and info. The icon is INSTANCE_SWAP (component property `icon`), so designers swap to any other Syntropy icon per instance.

> **Info:** Per-tone icon defaults: neutral → Icon/info · info → Icon/info · success → Icon/check-circle · warning → Icon/alert-triangle · error → Icon/x · brand → Icon/star. These are component defaults - change per-instance via the `icon` property (INSTANCE_SWAP) when context calls for it (e.g. swap success default to Icon/shield-check for compliance contexts, swap brand default to Icon/bookmark-star for saved/favorited).

> **Info:** When HasIcon=false, the pill is text-only. Use for compact labels where the icon would be visual noise - "Active", "Beta", abbreviation-style labels. The auto-layout collapses cleanly with no gap.

### Direction - LTR + RTL

Every variant exists in LTR and RTL. LTR uses IBM Plex Sans Medium; RTL uses Noto Sans Arabic Medium (same fallback as Badge and Tooltip - IBM Plex Sans Arabic is not installed in this file). The icon moves to the trailing edge in RTL so it sits at the start of the reading direction.

LTR →

RTL →

> **Tip:** In RTL the icon swaps to the trailing edge automatically - this is the auto-layout doing the work, not per-instance configuration. Designers don't need to flip anything; just pick the Direction variant that matches the page direction.

### Content guidance

StatusPill is a label, not a sentence. Keep copy ruthlessly short and use established conventions.

### Length and form

- One or two words. Three at most. "Approved", "Featured", "Pending review", "Action required".
- Single concept per pill. Don't cram "Pending review + late" into one label - split into multiple pills or pick the dominant state.
- Use the same casing as surrounding UI. Title Case for proper nouns and labels ("Featured"), sentence case for in-prose labels ("Action required").
- Arabic copy should be equally terse: "معتمد" (approved), "مميّز" (featured), "مرفوض" (rejected). Don't translate verbosely.

### When to use StatusPill

- Profile attributes - "Verified", "KYC complete", "Premium member", "VIP".
- Content metadata - "Featured", "New", "Editor's pick", "Sponsored".
- Compliance markers - "Sharia-certified", "Government-backed", "Insured", "CMA-regulated".
- Document/process attributes - "Draft", "Signed", "Expired", "Approved".
- Permission/role labels - "Admin", "Read-only", "Restricted".
- KPI deltas - "↑12%" with success tone, "↓3%" with warning, etc. (Often paired with the Stat component planned for 04f.)

### When NOT to use StatusPill

- For issuance lifecycle states (Raising, Funded, Defaulted, Repaid, etc) - use IssuanceStatusBadge. Locked palette, locked copy, audience-specific resolver, CI-tested invariants. StatusPill has none of that.
- For navigation items - use Tag (04a) or button-style chips.
- For form field validation states - use FormField error/success states, not a separate StatusPill next to the input.
- For interactive filters that toggle on/off - use Tag (04a) with clickable behavior. StatusPill is read-only.

Reference implementations. Real production code lives in lib/design_system/status_pill/.

### Basic usage

```dart
// Default pill - neutral tone, subtle variant, md size, no icon
SafqahStatusPill(
  label: 'Draft',
)

// Success with icon (uses default Icon/check-circle)
SafqahStatusPill(
  label: 'Approved',
  tone: StatusPillTone.success,
  hasIcon: true,
)

// Solid variant for high-emphasis surfaces
SafqahStatusPill(
  label: 'Featured',
  tone: StatusPillTone.brand,
  variant: StatusPillVariant.solid,
  hasIcon: true,
)

// Compact size for table cells
SafqahStatusPill(
  label: 'Active',
  tone: StatusPillTone.success,
  size: StatusPillSize.sm,
)

// Custom icon (swap from default)
SafqahStatusPill(
  label: 'Sharia-certified',
  tone: StatusPillTone.brand,
  icon: SyntropyIcons.shieldCheck,  // swap from default Icon/star
)
```

### Tone selector

```dart
// File: lib/design_system/status_pill/tone.dart
enum StatusPillTone {
  neutral,
  info,
  success,
  warning,
  error,
  brand;

  /// Per-tone default icon. Override via the icon: parameter on SafqahStatusPill.
  IconData get defaultIcon {
    switch (this) {
      case StatusPillTone.neutral: return SyntropyIcons.info;
      case StatusPillTone.info:    return SyntropyIcons.info;
      case StatusPillTone.success: return SyntropyIcons.checkCircle;
      case StatusPillTone.warning: return SyntropyIcons.alertTriangle;
      case StatusPillTone.error:   return SyntropyIcons.x;
      case StatusPillTone.brand:   return SyntropyIcons.star;
    }
  }

  /// Color tokens for subtle variant: {bg, text, border}
  StatusPillColors subtleColors(BuildContext context) {
    final theme = SyntropyTheme.of(context);
    switch (this) {
      case StatusPillTone.neutral:
        return StatusPillColors(bg: theme.bg.base, text: theme.text.muted, border: theme.border.default_);
      case StatusPillTone.info:
        return StatusPillColors(bg: theme.bg.infoSubtle, text: theme.text.info, border: theme.border.info);
      case StatusPillTone.success:
        return StatusPillColors(bg: theme.bg.successSubtle, text: theme.text.success, border: theme.border.success);
      case StatusPillTone.warning:
        return StatusPillColors(bg: theme.bg.warningSubtle, text: theme.text.warning, border: theme.border.warning);
      case StatusPillTone.error:
        return StatusPillColors(bg: theme.bg.errorSubtle, text: theme.text.error, border: theme.border.error);
      case StatusPillTone.brand:
        return StatusPillColors(bg: theme.bg.brandPrimarySubtle, text: theme.text.brandPrimary, border: theme.border.brandPrimary);
    }
  }
}
```

### Component implementation

```dart
// File: lib/design_system/status_pill/safqah_status_pill.dart
class SafqahStatusPill extends StatelessWidget {
  final String label;
  final StatusPillTone tone;
  final StatusPillVariant variant;
  final StatusPillSize size;
  final IconData? icon;
  final bool hasIcon;

  const SafqahStatusPill({
    super.key,
    required this.label,
    this.tone = StatusPillTone.neutral,
    this.variant = StatusPillVariant.subtle,
    this.size = StatusPillSize.md,
    this.icon,
    this.hasIcon = false,
  });

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final colors = variant == StatusPillVariant.subtle
      ? tone.subtleColors(context)
      : tone.solidColors(context);
    final effectiveIcon = icon ?? tone.defaultIcon;
    final isRtl = Directionality.of(context) == TextDirection.rtl;

    final children = <Widget>[
      if (hasIcon)
        Icon(effectiveIcon, size: size.iconSize, color: colors.text, semanticLabel: null),
      Text(label, style: TextStyle(
        fontSize: size.textSize,
        height: size.lineHeight / size.textSize,
        fontWeight: FontWeight.w500,
        color: colors.text,
      )),
    ];

    return Container(
      padding: EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: size.padX, vertical: size.padY),
      decoration: BoxDecoration(
        color: colors.bg,
        borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(999),  // Radius/Full
        border: colors.border != null
          ? Border.all(color: colors.border!, width: 1)
          : null,
      ),
      child: Row(
        mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
        children: hasIcon && isRtl ? children.reversed.toList() : children,
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

### Do and Don't

Five pairs of operational guidance for StatusPill usage.

### Match tone to semantic intent

- **Do** · Scenario name: Use success tone for genuinely positive outcomes (Approved, Verified, Connected). Use warning for things needing attention (Pending, Expiring). Use error for failed states (Rejected, Failed). The tone IS the meaning - don't pick by color preference.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't use success green just because green is the brand color, or error red just to grab attention. If overused, error red loses its weight and users start ignoring critical states.

### Use brand sparingly

- **Do** · Scenario name: Reserve brand tone for editorial promotion - Safqah-distinguished items like "Featured", "Premium", "Top performer", "Recommended". A handful per surface, never more.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't use brand tone for ordinary success states (use success). Don't use it on every card or it stops feeling distinguished.

### Subtle for inline, solid for emphasis

- **Do** · Scenario name: Use subtle variant in tables, list rows, deal cards, anywhere the pill is one chunk among many. Use solid in dashboard hero KPIs, callout banners, surfaces where the pill IS the story.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't mix subtle and solid in the same dense layout - pick one variant per UI context. Mixing creates an uneven visual rhythm.

### StatusPill is not a Badge

- **Do** · Scenario name: For issuance lifecycle (Raising, Funded, Defaulted, Repaid, etc), use IssuanceStatusBadge - it has audience-asymmetric copy, locked palette, and CI-tested invariants. StatusPill is for attribute labels OUTSIDE the lifecycle.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't recreate "Raising" or "Funded" as a StatusPill, even if it would visually match. The badge family encodes specific business rules that the pill family doesn't.

### Keep copy terse

- **Do** · Scenario name: One or two words. "Approved", "Pending", "Featured", "Premium member". Use established conventions ("New", "Active", "Expired") - don't reinvent.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't put sentence fragments in a pill ("Currently being reviewed by ops") - the pill becomes too wide and breaks dense layouts. Move that copy to a tooltip or detail surface.

### Notes from the maintainer

Design decisions, known gaps, and constraints for the next maintainer.

> **Info:** Neutral tone uses bg/base + text/muted + border/default (subtle) and bg/inverse + text/inverse (solid). Unlike the other 5 tones, there's no `bg/neutral-subtle` or `text/neutral` token in Syntropy - neutral falls back to generic semantic tokens. This is intentional: neutral pills should feel like part of the surrounding surface, not their own color family.

> **Info:** Per-tone default icons (success → check-circle, warning → alert-triangle, error → x, brand → star, neutral/info → info) are hardcoded into each variant. The `icon` INSTANCE_SWAP property lets designers override the default per-instance - useful when context calls for it (e.g. success with shield-check for compliance, brand with bookmark for saved items).

> **Warning:** Brand tone is reserved for editorial. Don't reach for it for ordinary success states - that's what `success` is for. Brand should feel distinguished; if it appears on every card, that distinction disappears.

> **Info:** No dark mode yet. StatusPill has Light-mode-only palettes (same as Badge, Tooltip). The semantic tokens it binds to DO have dark mode definitions, so adding dark mode is mostly a verification exercise rather than a redesign. Reverify contrast for warning + brand subtle variants if dark mode is enabled.

> **Info:** Radius is Radius/Full (9999) - pure pill shape. Don't change this. The pill shape is what visually distinguishes StatusPill from Tag (squarish corners) and IssuanceStatusBadge (also pill but with locked styling).

> **Tip:** StatusPill is read-only - no hover, focus, or click states. If you need an interactive pill (filter toggle, removable chip), use Tag (04a). If users find themselves wanting to click a StatusPill, that's a signal the use case might belong in Tag instead.

> **Tip:** RTL icon flipping is handled by the auto-layout, not per-instance. When Direction=RTL is selected, the icon naturally moves to the trailing edge because of how the auto-layout children are ordered for each direction variant. Designers don't need to mirror anything manually.

> **Info:** Arabic font fallback (same as Badge, Tooltip): Noto Sans Arabic Medium. IBM Plex Sans Arabic is not installed in this Figma file. If installed later, regenerate all RTL variants.

> **Warning:** Don't detach StatusPill instances to customize colors or padding. If a real use case appears for a custom tone (e.g. a sukuk-specific purple for educational content), propose adding a new Tone option to the variant set - not a detached one-off.
